about:
Industrial Plastics of Mpls., Inc. (IPM) operates from Minneapolis, Minnesota, where it has spent over 50 years in the plastic injection molding business. The company refers to itself as a pioneer in the field, though no founding year or founder names are publicly disclosed.

IPM provides plastic injection molding supported by in-house tool design and construction as well as partner toolmaking for prototypes, short runs, and Class A production tooling. The shop also offers rapid prototyping through multiple methods and consulting on new product development and design for manufacturability. Tooling storage and maintenance are included as standard.

The company serves original equipment manufacturers across the United States in sectors that include non‑invasive medical, agricultural, recreational, and educational products.

IPM emphasizes a continuous improvement philosophy it describes as "finding a better way daily," which it says translates into competitive pricing and quality. An on‑time delivery guarantee covers routine production schedules, emergency orders, and just‑in‑time requirements.

name: Industrial Steel & Wire Co Llc
old_description: We Work Tirelessly To Earn Your Business. Every Order. Every Time.
about:
Industrial Steel & Wire Co. LLC (ISW) is a third-generation, family-owned wire distributor headquartered in Bristol, Connecticut. The company was founded in 1935 by Dr. Harry Furlong in Chicago, Illinois, as Industrial Steel Wire Company. It remains under the leadership of the Furlong family, with Dr. Brian K. Furlong serving as president.

ISW stocks and distributes a broad range of wire products—including stainless steel, carbon steel, music wire, basic wire, non-ferrous wire, cold-heading quality, and specialty grades—across six North American service centers totaling 400,000 square feet of warehouse space. The company provides value-added processing such as torsion straightening (diameters .0300–.1250 in), cut-to-length, slitting, tension leveling, and multiple packaging options (continuous coils, catch-weight coils, reel-less cores, reels, and spools).

ISW serves manufacturers across diverse industries that require spring wire, strip products, and cold-heading wire. Its customer base includes companies needing fast, flexible supply of wire for applications ranging from automotive and aerospace components to industrial machinery, though the company does not publicly list specific vertical markets.

The company emphasizes its “ISW Pledge” of service, trust, selection, and response—principles dating to Harry Furlong’s original goal of earning customer confidence with every order. Differentiators include one-hour quotes, same-day shipping on stocked items, and a network of six strategically located warehouses to ensure rapid delivery.

about:
Indy Solar Solutions operates from Indianapolis, Indiana, as a locally owned small business serving homeowners and businesses across the state. The company was founded to help Hoosiers take control of energy costs through clean, reliable solar power, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed.

The firm designs and installs custom solar photovoltaic systems paired with battery backup, handling every step from initial site assessment and 3D modeling through permitting, utility interconnection, and final activation. In addition to new installations, it offers a dedicated solar panel cleaning service using specialized equipment to maintain peak production. The team works with high-quality solar panels and battery storage hardware, and assists customers with financing options including $0-down programs and federal tax credit navigation.

Its primary customers are residential property owners in Indiana, though the company also references commercial projects of varying scale. Typical engagements range from single-family rooftop arrays to larger business installations, all tailored to the specific energy usage, roof geometry, and shading conditions of each site.

Indy Solar Solutions distinguishes itself by emphasizing local presence and direct communication, positioning itself as an alternative to national chains. It promotes transparent pricing, a single point of contact from design to energization, and a commitment to honest workmanship backed by a small-business ethos.

name: Indy Urban Hardwood Company
old_description: Handcrafted solid wood furniture for your home, office, restaurant, and more.
about:
Indy Urban Hardwood Company operates from Indianapolis, Indiana, where it was founded in 2017 by Brian Presnell. The venture began as a response to the emerald ash borer infestation that was killing the city's ash trees, with the goal of giving those trees a second life as studio furniture.

The company fabricates handcrafted solid wood furniture using 100 percent recycled lumber sourced exclusively from the Indianapolis metropolitan area. Its processes include urban milling, kiln drying, custom design and fabrication, and flattening services. Since inception, the operation has recycled hundreds of thousands of board feet across multiple hardwood species, though facility size and headcount are not publicly disclosed.

The furniture serves a range of public and private spaces, with concrete examples including office buildings, libraries, restaurants, and music venues throughout Indianapolis. Residential clients are also served, reflecting the company's broader market reach.

The founding mission centers on sustainability and high design, positioning the business at the forefront of a shift toward valuing reclaimed materials. As Presnell states, the aim is simply to "do a good thing and make good things."

about:
Informed Choice Insurance Agency operates from Vivian, Louisiana, though its licensed headquarters is listed in Sun City Center, Florida. The firm was founded on the principles of integrity, service, and education, though a specific founding year is not disclosed. No individual founders are named in public materials.

The agency provides personalized insurance advisory services across health, life, Medicare, and property & casualty lines. Licensed agents compare plans from multiple top-rated carriers side by side, explain coverage in plain language, and assist with enrollment at no direct cost to clients—the agency is compensated by carriers. Services include Medicare Advantage, Supplement, and Part D plans; individual health, dental, vision, and long-term care policies; life insurance, annuities, and wealth management; plus home, auto, and commercial coverage. The team also supports Medicaid eligibility and durable medical equipment coordination. Ongoing annual reviews are a core offering.

Clients range from individuals, couples, and families to seniors, small-business owners, self-employed professionals, and retirees. The agency serves the broader insurance and healthcare sectors, with particular focus on Medicare-eligible populations and employer groups seeking employee benefits.

The company distinguishes itself through an education-first model that prioritizes clarity over sales pressure. Agents are directed to recommend solutions based on client needs rather than commissions, and the relationship continues after enrollment with claims assistance, plan updates, and future planning.

name: Infraredx
old_description: Makoto® is an intravascular imaging platform that combines high-resolution structural views with plaque compositional analysis to deliver unprecedented treatment insights.
about:
Infraredx, based in Bedford, Massachusetts, has been developing intravascular imaging technologies for nearly 30 years. The company was acquired by Nipro Corporation in 2015 and operates as a subsidiary within Nipro's Vascular Division. Founders are not publicly named; the current president and CEO is Stephen Sum, PhD, who joined the company as a senior algorithm scientist and advanced through R&D and regulatory roles.

The company designs and manufactures catheter-based imaging systems that combine intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) with near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS). Its flagship Makoto platform integrates high-resolution structural imaging with plaque compositional analysis, while the Clarispro HD-IVUS and Dualpro IVUS+NIRS systems address specific clinical needs. Essential accessories support the imaging catheters. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are disclosed.

Infraredx serves interventional cardiologists, hospital catheterization labs, and vascular researchers focused on identifying high-risk lipid-core plaques. The technology is used in clinical studies such as SPECTAL and COLOR, which supported 510(k) clearances. Customers include opinion leaders in cardiology who collaborate on defining new standards of care.

The company positions itself as a pioneer in conquering vascular disease, emphasizing the combination of structural and compositional imaging to provide unprecedented treatment insights.

name: Injection Molding Solutions
old_description: Our team at IMS has been in the plastics industry for all our professional lives.
about:
Injection Molding Solutions (IMS) operates from Siren, Wisconsin. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, though its team describes decades of collective experience in the plastics industry. Apothecary Products serves as the employer of record for IMS staff.

IMS provides plastic injection molding services with press capacities ranging from 15 to 500 tons and shot sizes from 0.1 gram to four pounds. The 80,000-square-foot facility supports micro molding, insert molding, lost core molding, and overmolding or multi-shot molding. In-house tooling capabilities include prototype and production tooling, augmented by hybrid tooling and parallel-path design methods that reduce lead times. Secondary operations cover assembly, painting, sonic welding, spin welding, pad printing, laser etching, inserting, lapping, and chrome plating.

The company serves consumer, medical, automotive, and defense sectors. Its mission emphasizes delivering high-quality plastic products and cost-effective engineering solutions to build long-term client relationships.

IMS highlights quick response to customer needs, innovative tooling that saves time and money, in-house tooling control, and a live person answering the phone as key differentiators.

about:
Innovative Circuits Inc operates from Corinth, Mississippi, providing contract electronics manufacturing services. The company’s founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm’s service portfolio includes product development and engineering support, printed circuit board layout and design for both surface-mount and through-hole applications, circuit board assembly, in-circuit and functional testing, reverse engineering of obsolete or discontinued products, prototype product design and PCB assembly, and finished product assembly and packaging. It handles production runs from prototype through small, medium, and high volumes, aiming to serve as a single-source electronics assembly partner.

The company serves customers in telecommunications, automotive aftermarket, and aviation industries. It is a member of IPC (Association Connecting Electronics Industries).

Innovative Circuits highlights its X-ray and optical vision inspection capabilities as part of its quality assurance, and positions itself as a partner from prototype to full production.

name: Integra Technologies
old_description: Over 40 years of helping hundreds of customers bring innovative products to market, we know how to take a wafer and turn it into a tested product.
about:
Integra Technologies operates from Wichita, Kansas, where it has provided semiconductor assembly and test services for over 40 years. The company was acquired by Micross in January 2025 and continues as an independent subsidiary.

The company delivers full turnkey semiconductor test and assembly services, covering die preparation (wafer thinning, dicing, pick-and-place, inspection), packaging and assembly (system-in-package, multi-chip modules, die attach, flip-chip interconnect, encapsulation), electrical test (wafer probe, singulated die probe, up-screening, custom ASIC/FPGA test), reliability qualification (PEM qualification, copper wire evaluation, ESD, CGA interconnect, burn-in, temperature cycling, thermal shock), destructive physical analysis, failure analysis, laser ablation, counterfeit detection, obsolescence management, and a parts management program. Mirrored assembly and test lines provide redundancy. Integra describes itself as the largest U.S. OSAT provider.

Integra serves the aerospace, defense, space, medical, automotive, and communications sectors, focusing on high-reliability applications where failure is not an option. As a DMEA DoD Source OSAT provider, it supports U.S.-based electronics manufacturers requiring secure, domestic supply chains.

The company emphasizes its end-to-end, 100% U.S.-based model as a differentiator, enabling tariff-free procurement, accelerated time to market, and lower costs through vendor consolidation. It states that no other competitor offers the same breadth of end-to-end solutions for the high-reliability market.
